notes: Phase was the main disagreement (about 30 percent): coders split general vs during-work for conduct rules on data, verification and research, and course-start vs before-course for the syllabus-statement contents. Rule: conduct rules for doing the work are during-work, the statement's contents are course-start, standing duties are general. Policy type: mandatory AI training (students, staff, all members, supervisors, 6 units) and compliance recordkeeping were typed P63/P54 by A and UNCOVERED by B; resolved to UNCOVERED because P63 covers only support for faculty and P54 only policy review. Other type splits: P56 vs P61 for scope and definitions (scope and defined terms go to P61), P65 vs P50 for the third-party risk review (P65), P50 vs P59 for approved tools when assessing (P50), P04 vs P11 for following each course's rule (P04), P09 vs P04 for the Statement Builder (P09). Modality: must vs should for the research documentation list followed the lead-in word 'should'. Stance: prohibit vs restrict on data-entry bans resolved to restrict because AI use itself stays allowed. A-only units (18) were kept after checking the text: definitions (Prompt), data rules, committee duties, and separate clauses; A's process tracking clause was split from detection tools. B-only units (2) kept; B's clause 'encouraging innovation, academic freedom' on the abstract page was dropped as part of the purpose sentence. Where coders anchored adjacent but different sentences (research disclosure vs venue compliance, review process vs affirm responsibility) they were counted as separate units, not as a match.
